pick.headline: U.S. and Libyan forces clash in the Gulf of Sidra
pick.summary: On March 24 and 25, 1986, U.S. Navy aircraft, operating south of Qadhdhafi's 'line of death' across the Gulf of Sidra, struck a Libyan missile site and sank or disabled several Libyan patrol boats after Libya fired missiles at them.
pick.significance: The clashes were the first armed round of the 1986 confrontation between the Reagan administration and Qadhdhafi. Within weeks came the Berlin discothèque bombing and the U.S. air raids on Tripoli and Benghazi.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of March 25, 1986, carried Belgrade TANJUG in English from Tripoli on high tension after the March 24 Gulf of Sidra clash, with Libya claiming three U.S. planes downed.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Eastern Europe, Vol. II No. 057, 25 March 1986
evidence.snippet: TENSIONS HIGH IN LIBYA FOLLOWING 24 MARCH CLASH LD251148 Belgrade TANJUG in English 1100 GMT 25 Mar 86 [Text] Tripoli, March 25 (TANJUG) -- Tensions in Libya are high since last night's clash in the Gulf of Sidra. Tripoli Radio, which is still the only source of official information on the incident, is broadcasting marches and calls for Arab unity and solidarity.
